title: Current revalidation repairs finite-component GRS QFT density provenance and reader drift
question: After certificate-hash drift and an obsolete T-054 note contract, do the existing finite-component GRS primary, independent and integrated lanes reproduce the declared scalar density theorem and its physical/parent firewalls?
method: Run the current finite-component GRS primary and independent scripts and compare their JSONs with the canonical child artifacts.
Classify the original integrated-reader failures as certificate-hash provenance drift and an obsolete live-task note contract, without editing EXP-000778 or its changelog event.
Refresh only the canonical child and integrated JSON artifacts and minimally update the reader to use the current live task plus append-only exploration/changelog ledgers.
Run the integrated verifier and assert exact source pins, child agreement, all-sixteen density/scope checks, the stronger-surface firewall, lineage, negative references and the current next gate.
Apply the QFT firewall: scalar density conclusions are not physical empty space, phase/state selection, the original 3D parent, Sector A or Pre-A.
finding: The primary lane passes 108/108, the independent lane passes 97/97, and the repaired integrated lane passes 170/170. The only pre-repair differences were the stored certificate hash and the requirement that a historical EXP ordinal and next gate remain embedded in the current T-054 note. Current source pins, canonical child/integrated JSONs, scalar-density scope and next gate now agree without changing the theorem boundaries.
decision_reason: This is a current reproducibility and protocol-reader repair, not a new theorem or gate closure. The finite-component GRS density bridge is restored as current evidence while the stronger surface estimate, physical reference, phase/state, original parent, C6, Sector A and Pre-A gates remain open.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing provenance/current-reader revalidation only. It does not alter EXP-000778, add a result card, prove an O(boundary) estimate, identify physical empty space, select a phase, derive a three-dimensional parent, or close Sector A or Pre-A.

adversarial_review.check: Fresh child outputs carry the current certificate hash and canonical artifacts equal fresh runs.
The reader uses current active-task plus append-only exploration/changelog semantics rather than a historical T-054 note string.
Scalar density equality remains distinct from state, phase, gap, physical-reference and full KMS conclusions.
The stronger cutoff-volume-interpolation O(boundary) estimate remains open and non-load-bearing.
No new exact proposition is introduced by this provenance repair; no artificial Lean theorem is claimed.

next_action: Attack the phase/physical-reference/one-dimensional-to-three-dimensional parent route with an explicit common parent, stress-tensor normalization and state/phase observables; retain the scalar density theorem and all physical firewalls.
